story.head: Iron sharpens iron
paras: The Mammoth (10-6-1) lost 5-4 in overtime to Montréal on Thursday, while the Senators (10-6-1) beat Buffalo 2-1 on Wednesday. Going in, the Mammoth are second in the Central (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Senators fourth in the Atlantic (tied for ninth).

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.618) says: their chances are worth about .730, and their goaltending has held them back. The Senators’ record (.618) is about what their chances are worth.

The Mammoth (1st) and the Senators (2nd) both rarely get pinned in their own end. The Mammoth roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (1st). As for the Senators, they play slow, tight games (3rd lowest) and get into more chippy games than almost anyone (3rd). Something has to give when the Mammoth’s shooting runs into the Sens’ defense. On top of that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Clayton Keller (4 G / 18 A / 22 P in 17 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Logan Cooley (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games. For the Senators, Tim Stützle (9 G / 13 A / 22 P in 17 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Drake Batherson (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 17 GP) is next in line.
Karel Vejmelka (6-5-0 / .868 SV% in 11 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Utah, but is expected to start. Samuel Ersson (2-3-1 / .880 SV% in 5 GS) is expected to go for Ottawa.

items.text: The Senators are newly without Ridly Greig, and have been without Linus Ullmark and William Eklund for several games. Samuel Ersson is expected to start.

The Mammoth are newly without Kailer Yamamoto and Nate Schmidt, and have been without John Marino since Oct 17. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
Tyler Kleven has missed the Senators’ latest game.
Logan Cooley has eleven goals on chances worth about 6.2 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
